newsitem.title: UK: Argos says same store sales up 8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Argos says same store sales up 8 percent.

text.p: British catalogue retailer Argos Plc said on Monday that like-for-like sales since the end of the first half of its accounting year were up eight percent.

But chairman Sir Richard Lloyd said in a statement that announced first half pretax profits of 28.1 million pounds ($45.3 million), down from 31.8 million a year ago, that current buoyancy in consumer confidence and overall retail sales "may not be sustainable."
Lloyd added that a stronger second half performance than that seen a year ago was expected, adding that the group was "well positioned to demonstrate continued growth in the year 1997 as a whole."
The company said that gross margin in the second half was "likely to be around 0.5 percent lower" than the year ago period, as a result of an "aggressively priced" catalogue.

Lloyd said that short to medium term earnings "may be affected by the investment in new organic business ventures," particularly in Holland, but added that the company was confident "for the longer term premium growth prospects."

Argos, which operates more than 400 catalogue showrooms around Britain, said that initiatives for developing sales, "with a view to improving market shares and thereby achieve a premium rate of like for like growth," were continuing.
